0.heading: Your current site is losing you customers
0.description: You pulled up your own site on your phone and watched it struggle to load. You closed it. Your customers do the same thing every day, and you never see those visits in your analytics.

1.heading: You're spending weeks on what should take days

2.description: You launched a page, got some traffic, and have no idea what happened next. No conversion data, no scroll depth, no way to know if the page is working or wasting your ad spend.

0.question: How long does it take to build a landing page?
0.answer: Most landing pages are live within 1-2 weeks from kickoff: a design review first, then the build in Next.js, performance optimization, and deployment to Vercel.

1.question: Can I update the content myself after launch?
1.answer: Yes. Your page can ship with a headless CMS like Sanity or Contentful so you can edit text, images, and sections without touching code. Alternatively, you get the Git repository handed off for developer-managed updates.

2.question: What's included in the SEO setup?
2.answer: Every landing page includes meta tags, Open Graph images, structured data (JSON-LD), sitemap generation, Core Web Vitals optimization, and semantic HTML. The setup also covers Google Search Console and analytics tracking.

3.question: What makes your approach different from a page builder or template?
3.answer: Templates give you a starting point. You get a finished product. Every page is custom-designed for your brand, hand-optimized for Core Web Vitals, and deployed on infrastructure that scales. You own the source code.

landingPages.approach: Everything starts with your conversion goal and works backward. Every layout decision, copy block, and interaction is designed to move visitors toward one clear action. The page is built in Next.js with a performance budget and deployed on Vercel's edge network so it stays fast across devices.
landingPages.outcome: A production-ready page with a 90+ PageSpeed target, clear analytics, and visibility into what visitors actually do. You own the code, and you can iterate on it without being locked into a subscription.

wordpressMigration.title: WordPress and legacy migrations
wordpressMigration.tagline: Move brittle sites to a faster Next.js foundation.
wordpressMigration.description: Rebuild brittle CMS, plugin-heavy, or legacy websites as fast Next.js applications while preserving SEO-critical content, URLs, forms, and editing workflows.

features.1: Next.js static generation with a 90+ PageSpeed target

deliverables.0: A Next.js rebuild of your site, built to a 90+ PageSpeed score target
deliverables.1: A redirect map that carries your existing rankings through the switch
deliverables.2: An editing workflow your team can use without touching code
deliverables.3: Documentation for the new stack, written for the person who maintains it
deliverables.4: Post-launch support while the new site settles in

0.heading: Your WordPress site is costing you every day
0.description: Plugin subscriptions, managed hosting, developer bills for routine updates. Add it up and your WordPress site costs more per year than rebuilding it once in Next.js.

1.heading: Slow speed is killing your conversions
1.description: Run your own site through PageSpeed Insights. If you're on WordPress, you already know what the score looks like. Every second of load time costs you visitors who will never come back.

2.heading: Security patches are a full-time job
2.description: Another week, another plugin update. Another security advisory you're not sure applies to you. Static sites built in Next.js don't have a plugin layer to exploit.

0.question: Will I lose my SEO rankings during migration?
0.answer: Migration risk is reduced with URL mapping, 301 redirects, metadata preservation, sitemap review, performance checks, and post-launch monitoring. Rankings can still move during a migration, so the cutover is planned carefully.

1.question: Can I keep my WordPress content workflow?
1.answer: Yes. Your site can connect to a headless CMS that feels similar to WordPress but serves content through Next.js. You keep the familiar editing experience with dramatically better frontend performance.

2.question: How long does a typical migration take?
2.answer: Simple brochure sites: 2-3 weeks. E-commerce or complex sites with custom plugins: 4-6 weeks. Both sites run in parallel during migration, with the cutover planned to minimize downtime.

3.question: What happens to my WordPress plugins?
3.answer: Each plugin is audited and replaced with a modern equivalent. Contact forms become API routes, SEO plugins become built-in Next.js metadata, analytics move to PostHog or GA4, and caching becomes unnecessary with static generation.

4.question: What does the first week of a migration actually look like?
4.answer: Day one is a full audit of your existing site: pages, plugins, SEO structure, and hosting costs. By day three, you see a working prototype in Next.js with your content and branding. The rest of week one is refinement, redirect mapping, and performance benchmarking. You're involved at every step, but you don't have to manage the process.

wordpressMigration.approach: A full audit of your WordPress site comes first: every page, plugin, redirect, and SEO signal. Then the site is rebuilt in Next.js with static generation, preserving your content and branding while reducing the maintenance overhead. Redirects are mapped, metadata is preserved, and rankings are monitored after launch.
wordpressMigration.outcome: A site that loads quickly, targets 90+ on PageSpeed, and requires much less maintenance. No more constant plugin updates, recurring security patches, or hosting fees that creep up every year. Your content stays exactly where Google expects it.

0.question: What does the AI automation prototype include?
0.answer: It includes process mapping, data and review requirements, a scoped working prototype, test cases with realistic examples, and a production build plan for the smallest useful automation.

1.question: Is this consulting or implementation?
1.answer: Both, in a deliberately small scope. The consulting is tied to a working prototype, so the recommendation is based on the actual workflow rather than generic AI advice.

2.question: Do you also build the production version?
2.answer: Yes, when the prototype proves the workflow is worth automating. The next step is usually a production build with monitoring, fallbacks, permissions, and clear ownership.

3.question: What makes a workflow a good candidate?
3.answer: The best candidates are frequent, costly, and reviewable: document intake, routing, enrichment, reporting, research, content operations, or handoffs where a human still approves the result.

aiConsulting.approach: We choose one repeatable workflow, map inputs, decisions, exceptions, and review points, then build a small prototype against realistic examples. The goal is not a demo with perfect sample data. It is a practical test of whether AI can remove work safely and what the production system would require.
aiConsulting.outcome: You leave with a prototype your team can inspect, a clear recommendation on whether to build, and a production plan for the smallest useful automation.

deliverables.0: An MVP your first users can sign up for, running in production rather than staging
deliverables.1: Source code you own outright, documented for the next developer or CTO

deliverables.4: A demo environment stable enough to put in front of investors

0.heading: You're building too much before validating
0.description: Six months of development with no user feedback is a recipe for building the wrong product. An MVP puts real data in your hands in weeks, before your assumptions turn into expensive mistakes.

1.description: Every month spent building features that don't matter is money you can't get back. Focus your budget on the core value proposition first.

0.question: What is included in the MVP plan?
0.answer: The minimum feature set needed to validate your idea with real users. This typically includes auth, core workflows, a database, deployment, and basic analytics. The first version stays limited to the features that prove the idea.

1.question: Can I scale the MVP into a full product later?
1.answer: Absolutely. Every MVP is built with production-grade architecture from day one: TypeScript, proper database schema, CI/CD, and monitoring. The codebase is designed to grow, not to be thrown away.

2.question: Do you help with product strategy or just development?
2.answer: You get help planning features and prioritizing what to build first based on your goals. The core service is development, but product thinking is part of every engagement.

3.question: How do you decide what to cut from an MVP?
3.answer: One question decides it: does this feature help you learn something about your users? Features that do not answer that question go on the post-launch list. The goal of an MVP is useful data from real users. Most founders are surprised by how little you need to start learning.

mvpDevelopment.approach: Your idea gets stripped down to its core hypothesis, and only what you need to test it gets built. Three weeks from kickoff, you have a working product in front of real users. The stack is Next.js and Vercel, so deployment is instant and iteration cycles stay short.
mvpDevelopment.outcome: A live product with real user data telling you what works and what doesn't. You stop guessing about product-market fit and start making decisions based on evidence. The codebase is clean enough to scale when you're ready.

1.description: Building a production-grade application requires architectural decisions that compound over years. You need a team that thinks about scale, security, and maintainability from day one.

2.heading: Off-the-shelf tools don't fit your workflow
2.description: You've tried Zapier, Airtable, and a dozen no-code tools. They got you started, but now you need custom software that works exactly the way your business does.

0.question: What's your tech stack for full-stack applications?
0.answer: Next.js and React for the frontend, PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM for the database, tRPC for type-safe APIs, Better Auth for authentication, and Vercel for deployment. Monitoring runs on Sentry and PostHog.

1.question: Do you handle hosting and DevOps?
1.answer: Yes. Projects deploy to Vercel with automatic CI/CD, staging environments, monitoring and alerting, and managed infrastructure. You get a fully operational production environment from day one.

2.question: Can you integrate with our existing systems?
2.answer: Yes. APIs and integrations for payment processors (Stripe), email services (Resend), CRMs, ERPs, and custom internal tools can be connected. If it has an API, it can usually be integrated.

3.question: Why do you build everything on Next.js?
3.answer: It handles frontend, backend, and API routes in a single codebase. That means fewer moving parts, faster iteration, and one deployment pipeline instead of three. For most web applications and SaaS products, it's the fastest path from idea to production without sacrificing long-term flexibility.

fullStackApps.approach: Architecture comes first: data model, API contracts, and deployment strategy. The build then proceeds incrementally with type safety end-to-end, so every layer of your application speaks the same language.
fullStackApps.outcome: A production-grade application with documented critical flows, tests for the agreed risks, and infrastructure planned for the expected load. The codebase stays clear enough for future improvements.

vitalExplanations.FCP: First Contentful Paint: how quickly visitors see the first content. A slow FCP means users stare at a blank screen and are more likely to leave before your page even appears.
vitalExplanations.LCP: Largest Contentful Paint: when the main content becomes visible. If this takes longer than 2.5 seconds, roughly half of mobile visitors will leave before seeing your message.
vitalExplanations.TBT: Total Blocking Time: how long the page is unresponsive to clicks and taps. High blocking time means frustrated users who tap buttons and nothing happens.
vitalExplanations.CLS: Cumulative Layout Shift: how much the page layout jumps around while loading. Shifting content causes users to accidentally click the wrong thing, damaging trust.
vitalExplanations.SI: Speed Index: how quickly the visible area of your page is populated. A slow Speed Index means your site feels sluggish even if it eventually loads.
vitalExplanations.default: This metric affects how users perceive your site's speed and responsiveness.

intro.name: Sebastian Kehle
intro.tagline: I design, build, and automate custom software.
intro.description: I've been building things on the internet for about ten years. While working in design and marketing I taught myself JavaScript and React and became a software engineer — and the contract work I started on the side grew into a design-first studio for custom software and AI automation.

paragraphs.0: I studied visual communication and design in Berlin and spent my early career in agencies, building websites and campaigns that connected creative work with business outcomes. That foundation in design thinking still shapes every project at webvise.
paragraphs.1: In 2017, I took on the CEO role at a recruiting technology company, where I raised funding and led the team in designing and implementing the core matching algorithm. Running a startup taught me what it takes to ship fast under real constraints.
paragraphs.2: I founded webvise in 2016. What started as a design studio evolved into a full-stack practice delivering web applications, branding, and AI automation for businesses across the globe.
paragraphs.3: Before webvise became the current studio, I led product and engineering work across startups and client teams. That shaped the delivery model I use today: scoped systems, fast shipping, and direct ownership.
paragraphs.4: My current work focuses on production AI engineering: LLM-assisted internal tools, automation pipelines, and software systems that people use in real operations. That practical experience shapes how webvise approaches AI projects: start with the workflow, define the controls, ship a system the team can run.
paragraphs.5: In 2025, I collaborated with a team spanning Bangkok and Berlin to build an AI-powered game engine extension, further deepening my applied AI expertise. Today, webvise combines everything I have built across design, engineering, product, and AI into a practice that ships production software in weeks.

internalTools.title: Internal tools and dashboards
internalTools.description: Dashboards and admin tools for managing data, workflows, users, and operations in one place.

detail.metaDescription: Custom internal tools, admin dashboards, reporting interfaces, and operational software, designed and built by one accountable engineer.
detail.timeline: Focused tools can ship quickly. Larger operational systems are planned in phases before implementation.
detail.approach: The work starts by mapping the operational workflow, the people involved, the decisions they make, and the systems that already hold the data. From there, the interface, backend logic, permissions, and integration layer are designed as one product.
detail.outcome: Your team gets a practical operations system that replaces spreadsheets, scattered admin screens, and manual handoffs with one reliable application.
capabilities: Role-based admin dashboards for teams, managers, and operators.
Editable data tables with filtering, search, bulk actions, and audit-friendly changes.
Internal CRM views for leads, customers, members, partners, or suppliers.
Reporting dashboards that combine operational data into useful decisions.
Workflow status views for approvals, assignments, queues, and handoffs.
Integrations with forms, CRMs, databases, email, analytics, and existing tools.
modules: Login, permissions, and team roles.
Dashboard overview with the metrics that matter.
CRUD interfaces for operational data.
Search, filters, sorting, exports, and activity history.
Notifications, assignment flows, and approval steps.
Deployment, monitoring, and post-launch improvement support.
outcomes: Operational data moves out of spreadsheets into one place your team trusts
Every task and record has an owner and a next step visible to everyone
Reports come from the system itself, with the copy-paste step gone
The tool grows with the workflow instead of being rebuilt every two years

faq.question: Can you replace our spreadsheets or Airtable base?
faq.answer: Yes. Spreadsheet-driven operations can become a custom application with roles, validation, workflows, reporting, and integrations while preserving the useful parts of your current process.

faq.question: Can this connect to our existing tools?
faq.answer: Usually yes. Common integrations include CRMs, forms, email platforms, analytics tools, databases, payment systems, and internal APIs. Integration effort is planned before the build starts.

faq.question: Do you also design the UX?
faq.answer: Yes. The same engineer works on workflow understanding, UX structure, backend logic, and deployment, so the interface is designed around real operational decisions.

aiWorkflows.title: AI agents with review gates
aiWorkflows.description: Tool-using agents for bounded tasks, with queues, monitoring, and approval where risk requires it.

detail.metaDescription: Agentic workflow automation with human review for document processing, triage, approvals, reporting, content operations, and internal handoffs.
detail.timeline: Planned around workflow risk. Prototype first when model behavior needs validation.
detail.approach: The work starts by separating what AI should draft, classify, extract, or suggest from what a person should approve. The review loop, data flow, prompts, model calls, fallbacks, and operational interface are then designed around that boundary.
detail.outcome: Your team gets a faster workflow without handing important judgement to a black box. AI handles repetitive steps, people stay responsible for decisions.
capabilities: Document extraction and structured data capture from messy inputs.
Support, lead, or request triage with confidence-aware routing.
Approval queues where AI drafts and humans review before action.
Reporting drafts, summaries, and internal handoff notes.
RAG systems and custom assistants grounded in your own knowledge base.
Monitoring, logging, and fallback paths for production use.
modules: Input capture from forms, inboxes, documents, or databases.
Prompt, model, and tool orchestration for the specific task.
Human review interface with approve, edit, reject, and escalate actions.
Structured outputs saved back into the system of record.
Evaluation checks, confidence signals, and error handling.
Analytics for throughput, accuracy, and manual override patterns.
outcomes: Repetitive processing gets handled by the workflow, with people reviewing instead of typing
Response and handoff times shrink because routing happens automatically
Triage, extraction, and reporting come out consistent across every case
Every AI decision stays visible and reviewable, with overrides logged

faq.question: Do you build fully autonomous AI agents?
faq.answer: Only when the risk profile supports it. Most business workflows work better with human-in-the-loop automation, where AI drafts, extracts, classifies, or recommends and a person approves important actions.

faq.question: Can you use our documents or internal knowledge?
faq.answer: Yes. Retrieval-based workflows and assistants that use your approved knowledge sources can be built. Access control, data handling, and update processes are scoped up front.

faq.question: How do you avoid hypey AI experiments?
faq.answer: The project starts from the workflow and business outcome. If AI does not improve speed, quality, consistency, or cost in a measurable way, it should not be the centre of the build.

companyBrain.title: Company brain systems
companyBrain.description: Knowledge and memory systems for reusable decisions, documents, project context, and rules.

detail.metaDescription: Custom company brain, memory, and retrieval systems for teams that need reliable access to documents, decisions, knowledge, and operating context.
detail.timeline: Usually phased as source audit, prototype, evaluation, then production workflow.
detail.approach: The work starts by mapping where knowledge lives, who can trust it, who can change it, and what decisions it should support. From there, the memory model, retrieval flow, review process, and interface are built around the way your team actually asks questions and uses context.
detail.outcome: Your team gets a maintained source of operational memory instead of scattered documents, stale chat threads, and one-off AI answers nobody can verify.
capabilities: Knowledge bases that combine documents, notes, records, and structured context.
Retrieval workflows grounded in approved sources and permissions.
Decision memory for project history, operating rules, and recurring judgement calls.
Review queues for improving, approving, or retiring knowledge.
Assistant interfaces that cite sources and keep uncertainty visible.
Evaluation checks for retrieval quality, freshness, and answer reliability.
modules: Source inventory and permission model.
Document ingestion, cleanup, and metadata structure.
Search and retrieval interface for team workflows.
Review, approval, and stale-content handling.
Assistant layer with citations, confidence signals, and fallback states.
Monitoring for usage, gaps, and recurring unanswered questions.
outcomes: People find the current answer without asking the same person again
Decisions and source material stay connected instead of disappearing into chat
AI answers become reviewable because sources, gaps, and uncertainty are visible
The knowledge system improves as the team uses it

faq.question: Is this just a chatbot over our documents?
faq.answer: No. A useful company brain needs source structure, permissions, review workflows, retrieval evaluation, and a clear operating model. The assistant is only one interface on top of that system.

faq.question: Can it respect private or role-based knowledge?
faq.answer: Yes. Permissions and source boundaries are built into the plan, so users only retrieve the knowledge they are allowed to see.

faq.question: How do you keep the knowledge from going stale?
faq.answer: The system can include ownership, review states, stale-content signals, update workflows, and analytics that show which questions are not answered well yet.

portals.description: Secure portals and business apps with login, roles, files, forms, and workflow status.

detail.metaDescription: Secure customer portals, member portals, partner dashboards, onboarding portals, and authenticated business applications.
detail.timeline: Planned in phases when multiple user roles, integrations, or workflows are involved.
detail.approach: The work starts by defining who uses the portal, what they should see, what they can change, and what the business needs to manage behind the scenes. The portal is then designed as both a user-facing product and an internal operations tool.
detail.outcome: Customers, members, or partners get a clear place to complete tasks, submit information, access files, and follow progress while your team keeps control from the backend.

Authentication, roles, permissions, and protected routes.
Forms, file uploads, status tracking, and request workflows.
Admin backends for reviewing submissions and managing users.
Notifications, email flows, and reminders.
Integrations with CRM, payment, analytics, and existing business systems.
modules: Login and account management.
Role-based portal navigation and protected content.
Profile, onboarding, request, or application forms.
File areas, document uploads, and review states.
Admin dashboard for users, submissions, and workflow status.
Email notifications and integration hooks.
outcomes: Status questions answer themselves in the portal instead of arriving by email
A branded login experience that holds files, forms, and history in one place
Users see where their request stands without asking anyone
The portal becomes the base layer for the next digital service you launch

faq.question: Can you build portals with different user roles?
faq.answer: Yes. Roles and permissions are a core part of the portal plan, including what each user type can view, submit, edit, approve, or manage.

faq.question: Can users upload files and track status?
faq.answer: Yes. File uploads, review states, status timelines, notifications, and admin review screens can all be part of the build.

faq.question: Can the portal connect to our CRM or backend?
faq.answer: Yes. Integrations are planned around the systems you already use, such as CRM, payments, databases, email tools, analytics, and internal APIs.

booking.title: Booking and event platforms
booking.description: Booking and event systems for registration, reminders, check-in, participants, and admin work.

detail.metaDescription: Custom booking, registration, event, participant management, reminder, check-in, and admin backend systems.
detail.timeline: Focused booking flows can move quickly. Multi-step programs are planned around the full event lifecycle.
detail.approach: The work starts by mapping the full lifecycle: discovery, booking, registration, reminders, attendance, follow-up, reporting, and admin work. The system is then built around the rules and exceptions that generic booking tools usually miss.
detail.outcome: Participants get a smooth booking experience and your team gets a reliable backend for managing capacity, attendance, communication, and follow-up.
capabilities: Custom registration and booking flows for events, services, and programs.
Capacity rules, time slots, waitlists, eligibility, and participant data.
Automated confirmations, reminders, updates, and follow-up messages.
Check-in views and attendance tracking.
Admin dashboards for participants, events, sessions, and reporting.
CRM, email, payment, calendar, and analytics integrations.

Session, slot, capacity, and waitlist management.
Participant profiles and registration details.
Automated email reminders and status updates.
Check-in interface for the day of the event.
Admin reporting, exports, and integration hooks.
outcomes: Bookings, reminders, and waitlists run themselves once configured
Participant data arrives structured before the event and stays useful after it
Organisers control capacity, sessions, and check-in from one admin view
The platform matches your event model rather than forcing a generic flow

faq.question: Can this support multiple event types or locations?
faq.answer: Yes. Event types, locations, sessions, capacity rules, and registration flows can be modelled around your actual program structure.

faq.question: Can it send reminders and follow-ups?
faq.answer: Yes. Confirmation emails, reminders, status updates, follow-ups, and internal notifications can be part of the workflow.

faq.question: Can it include payments or CRM sync?
faq.answer: Yes. Payments, CRM sync, email marketing, calendars, analytics, and exports can be included as integrations.

websiteApps.title: Website workflow layers
websiteApps.description: Existing websites upgraded with forms, qualification flows, CRM handoffs, dashboards, and review screens.

detail.metaDescription: Add product and workflow layers to existing websites without turning the project into a full platform rebuild.
detail.timeline: Focused workflow layers can ship quickly. Deeper product behavior is phased around integrations, backend needs, and review states.
detail.approach: The work starts by identifying where the website stops being content and starts creating work for the business. That workflow is then turned into forms, logic, integrations, dashboards, or review screens without forcing a full platform rebuild too early.
detail.outcome: Your website becomes the front door to a real business process: visitors submit better information, teams receive structured data, and follow-up work starts from a reliable system instead of an inbox.

Forms with validation, routing, notifications, CRM handoff, and analytics.
Conversion dashboards, reporting views, and lightweight admin screens.
AI assistants, content workflows, and automation rules where they remove manual work.
SEO, performance, accessibility, and deployment handled around the workflow layer.
A path from public website workflow to portal, dashboard, or full application when needed.
modules: Workflow map for the visitor action and internal follow-up.
Public form, intake, calculator, or application flow.
Validation, routing logic, CRM sync, and notifications.
Analytics, event tracking, and conversion reporting.
Dashboard or admin review layer for operational follow-up.
Performance, accessibility, SEO, and deployment setup.
outcomes: The site collects structured information instead of vague inquiries
Visitors move through a clear flow before your team gets involved
Follow-up work starts in CRM, dashboard, or automation instead of email threads
The workflow can later grow into a portal, dashboard, or full business application

faq.question: How is this different from a landing page?
faq.answer: A landing page mainly explains and converts. A website workflow layer captures structured information, routes it, connects it to business tools, and gives your team a way to review or act on it.

faq.question: How is this different from a full application?
faq.answer: It is narrower. The goal is to add the first useful product behavior to an existing website before committing to a broader portal, dashboard, or business application.

faq.question: Can it connect to CRM, analytics, or AI features?
faq.answer: Yes. CRM sync, analytics, notifications, AI assistants, admin review screens, and automation rules can all be included when they support the workflow.
